decisions.decision: Discovery is an intersection of three independently-sourced facts.
decisions.rationale: Who holds the block (content routing), who the node is (provider-signed certificate), what it can run (node-signed capability record). None is worth anything alone, and that is stated as a passing test: an attacker mints a perfectly valid capability record for an uncertified key and gains nothing. Splitting identity from capability lets a node re-sign locally when its engine changes rather than returning to the provider.

decisions.decision: Every exclusion is named and returned, never silently filtered.
decisions.rationale: Silent filtering leaves a requestor staring at an empty candidate list unable to distinguish a dead network from a wrong clock from a module nobody can run.

decisions.decision: The power-of-d sample is derived by rendezvous ranking, not drawn at random.
decisions.rationale: Same load-balancing result, but two requestors racing on one shard converge instead of doubling up, re-placement after a crash re-derives the same candidates, the ranking tail is already the re-pick list, and a placement decision can be replayed from the shard id and node set.

decisions.decision: Load is a hint; the offer is the authority.
decisions.rationale: A requestor load figure may be seconds stale, and treating it as truth is what makes several requestors stampede one node. LocalCapacity takes no ports and makes no calls, so "local information only" is a property of the type rather than a promise in a comment. A refusal is not an error path — it is how a stale guess becomes a correct decision.

decisions.decision: One eligibility gate, exported so there is exactly one of it.
decisions.rationale: eligibleNodes is shared by planPlacement and placeWithOffers. A second placer re-deriving eligibility would drift from the sovereignty rule. Falsified by planting the widening branch a refusal invites — "nobody allowed will take it, so ask someone else" — which probed 10 nodes instead of 2 and leaked a sovereign shard id into another owner fabric.

decisions.decision: A probe needs its own deadline, far below the RPC timeout.
decisions.rationale: An unreachable node cost a full RPC timeout before the re-pick, destroying the saving power-of-d exists to buy. Offers now carry a 2s deadline and silence is a stated refusal, so a dead peer appears in the rejection list beside a busy one. Only integration could show this — a unit test admission callback returns immediately.

decisions.decision: All nodes have equal functionality; the only difference is discovery.
decisions.rationale: No tier, no class, no lesser node. A browser cannot bind a listening socket, so it cannot be a seed a newcomer dials cold and must be found via a relay — but once connected, peers are indistinguishable, and a browser executes, stores, serves and takes quorum slots identically. Proven cross-device in Phase 3. Any decision keying on node kind is wrong; the only legitimate use is shared-dependency analysis over the discovery graph. Stated by the owner three times because the first two applications changed the vocabulary while leaving the mechanism discriminating.

decisions.decision: A seed contributes no discovery dependency, whatever relays it advertises through.
decisions.rationale: Only a node whose sole discovery path is a relay depends on it. Two certificates with identical relayIds therefore get opposite quorum verdicts. Found by the owner questioning a summary table; the original rule read relayIds without consulting discoverability and refused independent quorums.

decisions.decision: Attestation strength is derived from certificates, never declared by a caller.
decisions.rationale: owner-attested / owner-domain / independent. Owner-domain and independent both show two replicas, so the count alone cannot distinguish them and the label must travel with the result. A caller able to assert 'independently verified' would eventually assert one that was not.

decisions.decision: Disagreement is reported, never voted on.
decisions.rationale: In execution, reduce, and quorum composition alike. At R=2 there is no majority anyway, and voting silently converts 'something is wrong' into 'the majority was right' — the event verification exists to surface.

decisions.decision: Sovereignty is structural, not a preference.
decisions.rationale: planPlacement narrows to the owner's nodes before load is consulted; no branch widens it. A sovereign shard with nowhere to run stalls. Verified by adding the forbidden relax-under-pressure branch and watching four tests fail.

decisions.decision: Derive topology, never agree on it.
decisions.rationale: The reduce tree is a pure function of sorted partial CIDs — zero messages, no leader, no consensus. HRW ranking is itself the fallback list. Repair is recompute from content-addressed inputs, not state transfer; a late duplicate dedupes into nothing.

decisions.decision: The kernel must never require crypto.subtle.
decisions.rationale: A LAN origin is not a secure context. multiformats/hashes/sha2 uses WebCrypto and silently broke every CID on any non-localhost page, while the node still started — so it failed at the first block rather than at join. Now @noble/hashes, pure JS, with a browser test that deletes crypto.subtle.

decisions.decision: Relay browser capacity is capped by inbound limits, not reservations.
decisions.rationale: INBOUND_CONNECTION_THRESHOLD is 5 per HOST and MAX_INCOMING_PENDING_CONNECTIONS is 10, both below the 15 reservation default. Per-host binds in production too: every volunteer behind one NAT shares the budget. Exceeding either kills the noise handshake and reads like a network fault.

next_action: Phase 7 — churn, stragglers and coordinator survival. Build on what Phase 6 left: rendezvous ranking already returns the full fallback order with no lookup, and repair is recompute from content-addressed inputs rather than state transfer. The debt to pay is threat model 19 — a node that accepts work in order to stall it has no consequence today, and closing that needs completion-time reputation, which is Phase 7 natural output rather than a separate feature.
context_notes: 571 tests green across node, browser (real Chromium) and e2e projects; tsc clean; 47/72 requirements; repository public; Pages deployed by hand with no workflow file (DEMO-04 holds). Phase 6 closed all 7 criteria: the static peer list every earlier phase leaned on is gone, and a requestor knowing one bootstrap peer plus a data CID discovers executors, places work with power-of-d, and dispatches it. Two lessons worth carrying: assert the property rather than the mechanism (a placement test named the HRW top-ranked node as the one that would be offered, when the placer offers the least-loaded of the sample), and any timing claim needs a test with a real endpoint in it. The owner node-equality rule held throughout — nothing in discovery or placement keys on what kind of node something is; the fallback chain keys on availability at this moment, and a test asserts a server and a browser fall back identically.
